_note: SAMPLE recap content, generated from the hypothesised draft.

feature.headline: Everybody Hoarded Something They Can't Start
feature.standfirst: Fifteen rounds, twelve rosters, and a league-wide refusal to count the slots on the lineup card.

sections.heading: Keshia Drafted A Quarterback Room, And A Waiting Room
body: Josh Allen, Matthew Stafford, Caleb Williams, Jared Goff, Tyler Shough. Five quarterbacks, four allowed on the roster, two allowed in the lineup on Sunday. That is a starter, a superflex, and a bullpen deep enough that somebody had to be cut before the season began. Shough has thrown NFL passes in the same quantity most of this league has. The appeal there is the depth chart, not the résumé, and the depth chart is in Louisiana, not in Keshia's flex spot.

Then came the tight ends: Kyle Pitts, Dalton Kincaid, Brenton Strange. Three men for one slot, and Pitts has been the guy who's about to break out for four straight autumns. The math is brutal. Eleven of Keshia's fifteen picks were quarterbacks and tight ends, positions that between them account for three starting spots. Somebody has to catch the ball in the other five.

sections.heading: Mike Went Full PKM On Passers
body: Jalen Hurts, Drake Maye, Dak Prescott, Jaxson Dart, Daniel Jones. Mike hit the roster cap of four quarterbacks and then took a fifth anyway, which is the fantasy equivalent of buying a sixth chair for a five-person table. Dart is a rookie who spent August learning where the huddle forms. Daniel Jones has been released by one team and is now the reason another one has a competent Sunday, which is a real story but not a story you need behind three other starters.

The follow-through was better than the setup. Tee Higgins, Terry McLaurin, Jakobi Meyers, Jayden Reed is a functional receiving corps. But the running back room is D'Andre Swift and a prayer. Whatever happens at the quarterback position in this league this year, Mike is insulated from all of it, including the good parts.

sections.heading: Jay's Team Forgot The Second Quarterback
body: C.J. Stroud, taken in the eighth round, is the whole of Jay's quarterback plan. In a format that starts two, that means the OP slot gets filled every week by a running back who scores like a running back while eleven other teams run two passers throwing for six a pop. Jay built a genuinely gorgeous skill group. Jonathan Taylor, Kenneth Walker, Chase Brown, Drake London, Malik Nabers, DeVonta Smith. And then left the highest-scoring position in the sport to a single point of failure.

There was also a late tight end binge nobody ordered: Tucker Kraft, then Evan Engram, then Darren Waller, who retired and came back and is now on his fourth act. Three tight ends, one slot, and still one quarterback.

sections.heading: Colin Went 4th And Inches On Tight Ends
body: Travis Kelce, Mark Andrews, Isaiah Likely, AJ Barner. Four tight ends is one more than the roster cap allows, so the league software and Colin were having different conversations. Kelce is 36 and openly discussed retiring before deciding not to. Andrews is the other side of the same coin, a veteran whose targets have been quietly redistributed. Likely and Barner are in the same building as each other, competing for the snaps that make either of them useful.

Meanwhile the quarterback plan is Jordan Love and Malik Willis, a starter and the man who backs him up. If Love plays every week, Willis is a bench ornament. If Love misses time, Colin's superflex is a Packers quarterback either way. That isn't a hedge, that is a hostage situation.

sections.heading: Doug's Dangerous Team Hoarded Running Backs
body: Bijan Robinson, Jeremiyah Love, Kyren Williams, Bucky Irving, Bhayshul Tuten, J.K. Dobbins, Rachaad White. Seven running backs, one of the eight allowed slots left empty, and exactly two spots in the Sunday lineup for them. Dobbins has spent his career being excellent for stretches and then absent for longer ones. White has been steadily losing his own backfield to Irving, and now Doug owns both ends of that argument, so one of his picks is actively hurting the other.

The receiving room is Rashee Rice, Stefon Diggs, Jalen Nailor and a rookie. Rice is talented and has a suspension attached to his name. Diggs is coming off a torn ACL. Behind Jayden Daniels, the second quarterback is Bryce Young, who has been benched by his own team and then reinstated by it. Dangerous, as advertised. Not always to the opponent.

sections.heading: Chenell Defends A Title With Old Legs
body: Christian McCaffrey and Breece Hall, both of whom have missed serious time in recent seasons, anchor the reigning champion's backfield. Then Nico Collins, A.J. Brown, DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman, a receiving corps with real ceiling and a shared history of the hamstring report. George Kittle at tight end is genuinely excellent and also 32 with a body that has absorbed a decade of blocking defensive ends.

The quarterbacks came in the ninth and twelfth: Geno Smith and Cam Ward, a journeyman on his third franchise and a rookie learning on the job. In a league where twenty-four passers start every week, the defending champ is running the two nobody else wanted to run. It is a bet that the ball goes to the players catching it. Sometimes it does.

sections.heading: Jesse Took Three QBs And No Receivers
body: Brock Purdy, Kyler Murray, Baker Mayfield. Three starting quarterbacks in three consecutive picks, which is admirably decisive right up until you notice the first wide receiver arrived in round seven. Ladd McConkey, Carnell Tate, Mike Evans. Evans is 32 and has been running the same route tree since some of this league's rookies were in middle school.

Then the backfield got weird: Jadarian Price, Jonathon Brooks, Josh Jacobs, Tyjae Spears. Brooks has torn the same knee ligament twice and hasn't taken a meaningful NFL snap since. Jacobs in the tenth round is the actual value of the draft, a starting running back who somehow slid past ten managers. Jesse found him. Jesse also found five running backs he cannot start at once.

sections.heading: The Round Where Everyone Panicked At Once
body: Rounds fourteen and fifteen: twelve defenses, then twelve kickers, in perfect lockstep, like a fire drill nobody called. Brandon Aubrey went 790 places ahead of where any list had him. So did Cameron Dicker. So did Harrison Mevis, Jason Myers, Ka'imi Fairbairn, Eddy Pineiro, Harrison Butker, Cam Little, Jake Bates, Tyler Loop, Cairo Santos, and a man genuinely named Trey Smack.

There is no shame in it. The last two rounds have to go somewhere. But it does mean that with five bench spots each and byes coming, every single roster in this league spent its final two picks on the two positions that get streamed. Twelve managers, one identical idea, executed simultaneously. The Lab Rats are nothing if not a hive mind.

teams.teaser: Jesse stacked quarterbacks nobody else wanted and running backs whose knees have their own medical files.
body: Jahmyr Gibbs opened the draft and everything after him is a reclamation project. Travis Etienne, Jonathon Brooks, Tyjae Spears, Josh Jacobs, Jadarian Price. That is six running backs, half of whom have spent more recent time in a training room than a huddle. Brooks in particular is a bet that a rookie season interrupted by knee surgery ends with a player, not a rehab update. Stacking bodies at one position is a strategy. Stacking bodies that keep breaking is a hobby.

Brock Purdy, Kyler Murray and Baker Mayfield is a quarterback room assembled entirely out of guys the league argues about at Thanksgiving. Two of them start every week here, so every Sunday Jesse has to decide which of three coin flips he trusts, and the wrong one sits on a bench that only holds five players total. Mike Evans and Ladd McConkey are real receivers. Carnell Tate is a hope. Gunnar Helm is the only tight end on the roster, which is one more than the lineup requires and zero more than it survives.

Then the last two picks: a defense and a kicker taken when the board still had 800 and 790 better options sitting on it. Brandon Aubrey kicks moonshots and Jesse paid a premium for the privilege, in a round where an actual backup tight end or a fourth healthy running back was free. The shape here is a great first pick, a pile of lottery tickets, and no plan for the weeks when three of them are inactive at once.

teams.verdict: Nine Running Backs, Two Quarterbacks, One Problem
teams.teaser: Doug drafted a running back convention and remembered receivers somewhere around the tenth round.
body: Bijan Robinson, Kyren Williams, Jeremiyah Love, Bucky Irving, Bhayshul Tuten, J.K. Dobbins, Rachaad White. Doug didn't build a backfield, he built a depth chart for a league that does not exist. There is one RB slot and one FLEX. Every Sunday, five or six of these players will sit and watch. Dobbins has been chasing durability his entire career and White was already losing his own job in Tampa. The bench holds five. Doug filled it with more of the same thing.

Jayden Daniels is a legitimate franchise cornerstone and Bryce Young is the other quarterback. That is the whole room in a format that starts twenty-four every week. Young has been benched, restored, and asked to carry an offense that hasn't given him much to carry with. If Daniels misses a game, Doug is starting Young twice, which is a sentence Carolina fans read with a flinch.

The receiver situation is thinner still. Rashee Rice is genuinely good and comes with a suspension attached to the front of his season. After that it is Stefon Diggs, Jalen Nailor and De'Zhaun Stribling. One aging, one a fourth option, one who hasn't caught an NFL pass. Then a defense and Cameron Dicker with 790 better players still available. Doug spent fifteen picks proving he really likes running backs and never once asked who was going to throw it.

teams.verdict: Five Quarterbacks, Nobody To Hand Off To
teams.teaser: Keshia cornered the quarterback market so thoroughly she forgot to draft anyone who runs the ball.
body: Josh Allen, Matthew Stafford, Caleb Williams, Jared Goff, Tyler Shough. Five quarterbacks, two slots, hitting the roster cap with room to spare. Allen and Stafford start. Williams and Goff sit there being perfectly startable quarterbacks on a bench that only has five chairs, and Shough is a rookie who hasn't proven he can hold a job. That is three of five bench spots spent on players who will be watched, not used, in a league where bye weeks come for everyone.

The running back room is Ashton Jeanty and Jordan Mason. That is it. Jeanty is a terrific rookie carrying an offense on his back and Mason is a change-of-pace back on a team that has better options. When either misses time, Keshia is starting a receiver at FLEX and hoping. There is no third back anywhere on this roster, which in a fifteen-round draft takes real commitment to avoid.

Kyle Pitts, Dalton Kincaid and Brenton Strange gives her three tight ends for one slot. Pitts has been the league's favorite unfulfilled promise for four straight years, Kincaid keeps getting hurt right when he gets going. Courtland Sutton and Khalil Shakir are solid, Makai Lemon is a rookie. Harrison Mevis went with 790 better players on the board. Keshia won the quarterback position by such a margin that she has nobody left to play the other eight.

teams.teaser: Chenell built a gorgeous skill-position roster and then filled the superflex slot with Geno Smith and Cam Ward.
body: Christian McCaffrey and Breece Hall is the most talented and most surgically documented backfield in the room. Both are elite when upright. Both have missed enormous chunks of recent seasons. Then A.J. Brown, Nico Collins, DK Metcalf, Michael Pittman. That is a receiving corps that would win a lot of leagues, and George Kittle is the best tight end available at the position when he stays in the lineup, which is a phrase that follows Kittle around like a shadow.

Now the quarterbacks. Geno Smith, taken in the ninth. Cam Ward, taken in the twelfth. Two starters required every single week. Geno leads the league in interceptions as often as touchdowns, and Ward is a rookie learning on a team that is going to make him learn the hard way. Chenell spent nine rounds building a superteam and then handed it to the two guys most likely to throw it to the other team. In a six-point passing touchdown format, that gap isn't cosmetic. It is the whole ballgame.

Jaylen Warren and Kenny Gainwell behind McCaffrey and Hall is at least sensible insurance. Chig Okonkwo is a fine second tight end. The Browns defense and Jason Myers arrived with roughly 790 better players still sitting there, which is the traditional close. The champion drafted like the champion right up until the position that decides this format, and then closed her eyes.

teams.verdict: Four Tight Ends, One Quarterback, Zero Chance
teams.teaser: Bree collected tight ends like commemorative plates and drafted exactly one quarterback for two slots.
body: Tyler Warren, Colston Loveland, Sam LaPorta, Greg Dulcich. Four tight ends. One tight end slot. Warren and Loveland are rookies who haven't caught a professional pass, LaPorta has been fighting his way back from a season that got away from him, and Dulcich has spent more time on injury reports than depth charts. Three of these players cannot start on the same Sunday no matter what happens, and they are occupying bench spots on a roster that only has five.

The quarterback situation is worse. Sam Darnold, alone, in the sixth round, for a format that requires two starters every week. Darnold has been given the keys by four organizations and returned them each time with the seat adjusted. When he has a bad week, and he will have bad weeks, Bree's OP slot is empty. Not weak. Empty. There is no second quarterback anywhere on this roster and the draft is over.

The receivers are genuinely excellent: Puka Nacua, CeeDee Lamb, Chris Olave when healthy, which is the eternal Olave qualifier. The running backs are a committee of Rico Dowdle, Kyle Monangai, Aaron Jones and Jacory Croskey-Merritt, which is four guys sharing two jobs across four cities. Ka'imi Fairbairn closed things out with 790 better players available. Bree drafted a fantastic flex roster for a league with different rules.

teams.verdict: Great Roster, One Quarterback, Four Tight Ends
teams.teaser: Jay assembled a beautiful set of skill players and then handed the whole thing to C.J. Stroud alone.
body: Jonathan Taylor, Kenneth Walker, Chase Brown, Drake London, Malik Nabers, DeVonta Smith. Through six rounds this is the cleanest roster in the draft, every pick a starter, no reaches, no lottery tickets. Nabers is coming off a season that ended early, and Walker has never played a full one, but the talent is real and the shape is right. Then the draft turns, and it turns hard.

C.J. Stroud is the only quarterback here. One. In a format where twenty-four start every week and passing touchdowns pay six. Stroud spent last season getting hit more than any young quarterback should and the offense around him hasn't obviously improved. If he has a quiet week, Jay doesn't have a quiet week. He has an empty roster slot. There was no second quarterback taken in fifteen rounds, so every Sunday the OP spot gets filled by a running back and a shrug.

Meanwhile: Tucker Kraft, Evan Engram, Darren Waller. Three tight ends for one slot, and Waller retired and then unretired, which isn't the kind of depth that wins a bye week. Marvin Harrison Jr., Xavier Worthy and Calvin Ridley add receiver bodies to a roster that already had six. Eddy Pineiro rounds it out with 790 better players available. Jay drafted the best half-roster in the room and then stopped.

teams.verdict: Eight Receivers, Nobody Runs The Ball
teams.teaser: Tyler drafted every wide receiver in America and exactly one running back to hand the ball to.
body: Ja'Marr Chase and Justin Jefferson is a top of the draft that most managers would trade a limb for. Then DJ Moore, Zay Flowers, Jameson Williams, Wan'Dale Robinson, Rashid Shaheed. Seven receivers, and the lineup has three slots for them plus a FLEX. Shaheed is coming back from a knee that ended his season, Jameson Williams has been a big-play threat and a headache in equal measure, and Wan'Dale Robinson catches nine passes for forty yards with alarming consistency. Volume at one position doesn't become value at another.

The backfield is Chuba Hubbard. Singular. Ninth round. That is the entire running back room on a fifteen-man roster with an RB slot and a FLEX that Tyler will now fill with a fourth receiver every week. Hubbard is a fine player on a bad offense, and when he sits, there is nothing behind him. Not a handcuff, not a rookie, not a Week 14 stab in the dark. Nothing.

Trevor Lawrence and Justin Herbert cover the two quarterback slots competently, which is the one structurally sound thing here. Jake Ferguson, Juwan Johnson and Terrance Ferguson give him three tight ends for one slot, using bench space he desperately needs for a running back who doesn't exist. Harrison Butker closed it out with 790 better players still on the board. Tyler built a receiving corps and forgot the rest of the team.

teams.verdict: Five Tight Ends And A Retirement Party
teams.teaser: Colin drafted five tight ends for one slot, including two Ravens who split the same targets.
body: Travis Kelce, Mark Andrews, Isaiah Likely, AJ Barner, and Tyler Warren's spiritual cousin. That is five tight ends on a roster with one tight end slot. Kelce is thirty-six and visibly no longer the player who broke the position. Andrews and Likely play for the same team and eat from the same plate, so Colin has guaranteed that whichever one he starts, the other one had the better game. Barner is a blocking tight end. That is four bench spots out of five, spent on a position that pays out once a week.

Saquon Barkley and Javonte Williams anchor a real backfield, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba is a legitimate WR1. Tony Pollard is a fine third back. But the receiver room after JSN is Tetairoa McMillan, a rookie, and Jerry Jeudy, who has spent his career being described as talented by people watching a different receiver make the catch. That is thin for a lineup that starts three.

Jordan Love and Malik Willis is the quarterback plan. Love is real. Willis is a backup who played four good games in relief and got drafted here like it was a career. Two starters required, one reliable option, and the fallback is a guy whose own team gave the job back the moment their starter was healthy. Cam Little arrived with 790 better players available. Colin drafted a tight end museum and forgot to staff the rest of the building.

teams.verdict: Two Quarterbacks, One Of Them Missing
teams.teaser: James drafted a strong, sensible roster and then trusted Joe Burrow's availability with the whole season.
body: Derrick Henry, Omarion Hampton, TreVeyon Henderson is a backfield with a genuine identity. One ageless bruiser and two young backs with real workloads coming. Trey McBride is a top-tier tight end taken at the right time. Garrett Wilson and Emeka Egbuka are legitimate starters. Through eight rounds this is one of the more coherent rosters in the room, which makes what follows more frustrating.

Joe Burrow is the quarterback plan and there is no second one. Not a backup, not a bye-week body, nothing across fifteen rounds. Burrow's last season ended on the turf with a wrist injury, and the format demands two starting quarterbacks every single week. James is starting Burrow and a running back in the OP slot from Week 1, which is a decision made before the season, not forced by it. Six-point passing touchdowns make that hole expensive every Sunday, not just the ones Burrow misses.

The back half wanders. Luther Burden, Michael Wilson, Matthew Golden, Jordan Addison. Four receivers with real questions between them, and Addison starts his season serving a suspension. MarShawn Lloyd has barely played, Oronde Gadsden is a rookie tight end. The Seahawks defense and Jake Bates went with roughly 790 better players available. The foundation here is strong enough that the missing quarterback stings more, not less.

teams.verdict: Four Tight Ends And Fifteen Injury Reports
teams.teaser: Justin drafted Lamar Jackson, then spent ten rounds collecting receivers who spend more time rehabbing than running routes.
body: Amon-Ra St. Brown and Lamar Jackson is a beautiful start, and Bo Nix in the third means Justin actually solved superflex before most of the room noticed it was a problem. That is the good news, and it is genuinely good. Then the roster turns into a waiting room.

Christian Watson tore his ACL and is chasing his way back. Brian Thomas Jr. and Chris Godwin both spent chunks of last season unavailable. Godwin's ankle was the kind of injury that ends seasons and follows players into the next one. Rome Odunze and Parker Washington round out a receiving corps that will be one bad Saturday from unstartable. Quinshon Judkins and David Montgomery are the backfield, which is two backs total for an RB slot and a FLEX, and Montgomery has never been the guy who finishes a season carrying a full workload.

Harold Fannin, Dallas Goedert and Dalton Schultz gives Justin three tight ends for one slot, using bench spots that a third running back should be occupying. Goedert has missed games in each of the last several seasons and Schultz is a possession tight end on an offense that runs through everyone else. The Steelers defense and Tyler Loop closed it with 790 better players on the board. Justin got the hard part right and then drafted a roster that needs everybody healthy at once.

teams.verdict: Six Quarterbacks, Two Running Backs, One Lineup
teams.teaser: Mike drafted a quarterback room deep enough to field a scrimmage and one running back to carry the whole offense.
body: Jalen Hurts, Drake Maye, Dak Prescott, Jaxson Dart, Daniel Jones. Five quarterbacks in six rounds, hitting the four-QB roster cap and then some, for a lineup with two spots. Hurts and Maye start. Dak sits on a bench with five chairs. Dart is a rookie who hasn't won a job and Daniel Jones has been cut loose by an organization that drafted him sixth overall and then paid to make him go away. Mike used a third of his draft to solve a problem he had already solved in round two.

D'Andre Swift is the running back. That is the sentence. One back, taken in the fifth, on a Chicago offense that has spent two seasons trying to find someone else to give the ball to. The RB slot and the FLEX both need bodies every week, and Mike has one body and a stack of quarterbacks who cannot be legally deployed there. When Swift has a nine-carry afternoon, there is no alternative anywhere on this roster.

Tee Higgins, Terry McLaurin, Jakobi Meyers and Jayden Reed is a perfectly respectable receiving corps that will be doing more work than any receiving corps should. Hunter Henry and Kenyon Sadiq cover tight end. Cairo Santos and the Texans defense came off the board with 790 better players available. Mike built a quarterback room, and not much else.

teams.verdict: Four Tight Ends And Aaron Rodgers
teams.teaser: Evan drafted the best pair of running backs in the room and then wandered into a tight end clearance sale.
body: James Cook and De'Von Achane back to back is the sharpest two-round open of the draft. Two backs with real volume on offenses that want to score. Patrick Mahomes and Brock Bowers next is exactly right too. Four picks in, Evan had the strongest core in the room and no obvious flaw. Then the draft went on for eleven more rounds.

Brock Bowers, T.J. Hockenson, Pat Freiermuth. Three tight ends for one slot, all of them startable, two of them permanently benched. Hockenson is coming off the knee injury that cost him most of a season and Freiermuth is a fine player who will never see Evan's lineup while Bowers is breathing. That is bench space that should be holding a third running back or a fourth receiver.

The receiver room ages fast: Davante Adams, Deebo Samuel and Alec Pierce, plus George Pickens and Jaylen Waddle. Adams is thirty-three and Deebo has spent recent seasons being described as a gadget, which is what happens when a player stops winning routes. Aaron Rodgers is the second quarterback, forty-one years old, on his third team in four seasons, and the last two stops ended with everyone involved looking relieved. Trey Smack closed it out with 790 better players available. Great start, long fade.
